rc.title: Reading Comprehension
rc.directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. Choose the most appropriate option.
rc.passage: Of all the casualties of the digital age, the most quietly devastating is our capacity for sustained attention. A century ago, an educated reader could lose himself in a dense novel for hours; today, even the committed reader finds his eyes drifting after a few paragraphs, his hand reaching, almost involuntarily, for the glowing rectangle in his pocket. The problem is not that we read less — by some measures we read more than ever — but that we read shallowly, skating across the surface of a thousand fragments rather than diving into the depths of a single idea. Technology companies, it must be said, have engineered this restlessness deliberately; their profits depend on our distraction. Yet to blame the machines entirely would be too convenient. The deeper truth is that sustained attention has always been difficult, always demanded a discipline that most of us would rather avoid. The screen did not create our impatience; it merely gave it a permanent home.

questions.question: Q1. Which of the following best expresses the central idea of the passage?
options: The financial success of technology companies in the digital age
The decline of our ability to concentrate deeply on a single idea
The superiority of old novels over modern forms of writing
The harmful physical effects of reading for too many hours
questions.answer: The decline of our ability to concentrate deeply on a single idea
questions.explanation: The passage repeatedly returns to the loss of 'sustained attention' and the habit of reading 'shallowly'. The other options are details or distortions, not the main concern.

questions.question: Q2. According to the author, the responsibility for our distraction:
options: lies entirely with individual readers and their laziness
is shared between technology and our own nature
cannot be determined from the available evidence
questions.answer: is shared between technology and our own nature
questions.explanation: The author admits companies 'engineered this restlessness' but adds that 'to blame the machines entirely would be too convenient', since 'sustained attention has always been difficult'. So responsibility is shared.

questions.question: Q3. As used in the first sentence, the word 'casualties' most nearly means:
questions.explanation: A 'casualty' is something destroyed or lost. The trap is confusing it with 'casual' (informal). The context — 'the most quietly devastating' — confirms the sense of loss.

questions.question: Q4. The author states that the real problem with modern reading is that:
options: people read far fewer books than they once did
people read shallowly rather than deeply
modern novels have become far too dense
technology has made reading almost impossible
questions.answer: people read shallowly rather than deeply
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says 'The problem is not that we read less ... but that we read shallowly.' Option (a) is directly contradicted.

questions.question: Q5. The overall tone of the passage can best be described as:
questions.explanation: The author criticises the loss of attention but resists easy blame ('too convenient'), weighing both sides. That balance is reflective and critical, not purely angry or indifferent.

cloze.title: Cloze Test
cloze.directions: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (SSC CGL 2024 PYQ)
cloze.passage: The beginning of the story is (1)______ in its presentation but (2)______ the style eases out and becomes haunting in its simplicity. The author brings out the human elements in his story. This common element of sympathy and sacrifice is given a new (3)______ by the old artist who shows by his last desperate act that one can be a hero for one day if only one cares (4)______. O Henry's treatment of his material is balanced and controlled, a fine (5)______ of humour and pathos.

questions.question: Blank (1):
questions.explanation: 'Quaint' means charmingly old-fashioned or unusual, fitting a distinctive presentation. 'Prone/habitual' suggest tendency; 'delectable' means tasty — both off-context.

questions.question: Blank (2):
questions.explanation: The style 'eases out' over time, so 'gradually' (slowly, over time) is correct.

questions.question: Blank (3):
questions.explanation: A 'new dimension' means a new aspect or perspective added to the theme of sympathy and sacrifice.

questions.question: Blank (4):
questions.explanation: 'cares enough' conveys sufficient concern to act heroically. The other words do not fit the idea of sufficiency.

questions.question: Blank (5):
questions.explanation: 'A fine blend of humour and pathos' means a smooth combination of the two — exactly the intended meaning.

rc.title: Reading Comprehension
rc.directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. Choose the most appropriate option.
rc.passage: The Indian state has not infrequently used the colonial offence of sedition, codified under Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), as a tool to quell dissent. In May 2022, the Supreme Court of India asked State and central governments to refrain from registering new first information reports and from taking coercive measures under Section 124A in S.G. Vombatkere vs Union of India while the Centre said it would “reconsider” the provision. When the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) took effect in 2024, Parliament effectively replaced Section 124A with Section 152 and increased the minimum sentence to seven years. It was sedition by a new name. In February 2026, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant orally observed that the Centre’s promise in 2022 to review the provision could not bind Parliament. As if to release the pressure on courts, but also effectively easing the country’s passage into the BNS era, on May 21, 2026, the Court said that if an accused person has no objection, courts may proceed on cases involving Section 124A. However, such consent from the accused may be coerced, especially if they lack robust legal representation, because the alternative for the incarcerated persons is indefinite delay. It is effectively a Hobson’s choice between bad and worse outcomes. Indeed, as the 2022 stay paused the use of Section 124A pending constitutional challenge, how meaningful an accused person’s consent to trial can be where refusal may entail prolonged delay is unclear. S.G. Vombatkere also provided those charged with sedition to move for bail, meaning liberty rather than restoring proceedings was the intended remedy for frozen trials. The May clarification swings in the other direction, and also stands in contrast to the ‘bail is the rule’ principle that the Court recently reinforced in Syed Iftikhar Andrabi. If the Court wished to preserve agency, it should have paired continuation with a presumption of bail. The 2022 stay was also intended to annul the chilling effect of the charge of sedition on free speech. Now, wealthier or politically connected accused persons may secure bail through sustained litigation and wait out proceedings outside the prison, whereas poorer prisoners who are unable to secure bail will be compelled to consent to a trial, if only to obtain a verdict. As a result, liberty could depend on the capacity to litigate rather than on legal principles. Finally, if the state knows that cases involving constitutionally contested offences can remain in limbo while the accused persons are incarcerated, there is a perverse incentive for bad-faith state actors to not resolve the underlying uncertainty quickly. Instead of determining once and for all whether sedition as a criminal offence is constitutionally sustainable, the Court has passed the burden to the accused and declined to do its own duty.

questions.question: Q1. Which of the following best expresses the central idea of the passage?
options: The history of sedition laws in colonial India
The Supreme Court's efforts to strengthen sedition laws
The concerns arising from allowing sedition trials to proceed based on the accused's consent
The need to increase punishment under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
questions.answer: The concerns arising from allowing sedition trials to proceed based on the accused's consent
questions.explanation: The passage primarily discusses the Supreme Court's May 2026 clarification and argues that consent may not be genuinely voluntary, creating unfair consequences for accused persons.

questions.question: Q2. Why does the author describe the accused person's situation as a 'Hobson's choice'?
options: Because the accused has several equally attractive legal options
Because the accused must choose between consenting to trial or facing prolonged delay
Because the accused can challenge the law in multiple courts
Because the accused can avoid trial altogether
questions.answer: Because the accused must choose between consenting to trial or facing prolonged delay
questions.explanation: The passage explains that refusal to consent may lead to indefinite delay, leaving the accused with only undesirable alternatives.

questions.question: Q3. According to the passage, what was the purpose of the Supreme Court's 2022 stay on Section 124A?
options: To pause the use of Section 124A while its constitutional validity was under review
questions.answer: To pause the use of Section 124A while its constitutional validity was under review
questions.explanation: The passage states that the 2022 stay suspended the use of Section 124A pending a constitutional challenge.

questions.question: Q4. Which of the following consequences does the author fear may result from the May 2026 clarification?
options: All sedition cases will immediately be dismissed
Only wealthy citizens will be charged under sedition laws
Liberty may depend more on a person's ability to litigate than on legal principles
The constitutional challenge to sedition will end quickly
questions.answer: Liberty may depend more on a person's ability to litigate than on legal principles
questions.explanation: The author argues that wealthier accused persons may secure bail and wait, while poorer accused persons may feel compelled to consent to trial.

questions.question: Q5. What is the tone of the author in the passage?
questions.explanation: The author criticizes the Court's approach, highlighting issues such as coerced consent, inequality, and unresolved constitutional uncertainty.

rc.title: Reading Comprehension
rc.directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. Choose the most appropriate option.
rc.passage: As India’s energy demands scale rapidly alongside its urban expansion, the country finds itself at a critical crossroads regarding sustainability. While the rapid adoption of green technology is encouraging, the heavy reliance on imported fossil fuels remains a glaring vulnerability. Policymakers are now tasked with a difficult balancing act: they must support economic growth while simultaneously enforcing strict conservation measures. True progress will not stem from technological breakthroughs alone, but from a fundamental shift in our daily consumption habits and urban planning strategies. If citizens and industries fail to recognize the urgency of this transition, the resulting environmental and economic strain will only accelerate.

questions.question: Q1. What is the main idea of this passage?
options: India has completely resolved its energy crisis through green technology.
Urban expansion is the only cause of environmental pollution in India.
India faces an urgent need to balance economic growth with sustainable energy and consumption habits.
The government should stop relying entirely on urban planning.
questions.answer: India faces an urgent need to balance economic growth with sustainable energy and consumption habits.
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes the challenge of balancing economic growth with sustainability, conservation measures, and changes in consumption habits.

questions.question: Q2. According to the author, what is considered a 'glaring vulnerability'?
options: The slow adoption of green technology
The heavy reliance on imported fossil fuels
The lack of citizen awareness about climate change
The rising costs of urban real estate
questions.answer: The heavy reliance on imported fossil fuels
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that the heavy reliance on imported fossil fuels remains a glaring vulnerability.

questions.question: Q3. In the context of the passage, what does the word 'sustainability' mean?
options: Using resources in a way that meets current needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs
The total halt of all industrial and manufacturing processes
Increasing the importation of fossil fuels to meet immediate demands
Completely rebuilding major cities to improve ventilation
questions.answer: Using resources in a way that meets current needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs
questions.explanation: Sustainability refers to responsible resource use that supports present needs while preserving resources and opportunities for future generations.

parajumble.title: Para Jumbles
parajumble.directions: Each sentence has been split into four parts (P, Q, R, S) given in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges them into a meaningful sentence.

parts.label: P
parts.text: When it gave way on Saturday, the structure was undergoing more illegal construction.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: Unauthorised floors, weak foundations, use of poor-quality materials and deviations from approved plans seem to have become commonplace in Delhi.

parts.label: R
parts.text: The building collapse in Delhi's Saidulajab that claimed six lives evokes a sense of terrible déjà vu.

parts.label: S
parts.text: The five-storey building shouldn't legally have had more than three floors.

items.explanation: R introduces the incident. S describes the building involved. P explains what was happening when it collapsed. Q concludes with a broader observation about illegal construction practices in Delhi.

parts.label: P
parts.text: Tesla has updated its panels to be about 10 percent more efficient, and has also lowered its prices.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: The company also engineers, manufactures and installs solar panels -- both the traditional kind and modules that look like ordinary roof tiles.

parts.label: R
parts.text: And while the latter seems like it could be a path to more mainstream adoption of renewable energy, the former is still the go-to solution for the solar industry.

parts.label: S
parts.text: Tesla doesn't just make cars.

items.explanation: S introduces Tesla's broader business. Q explains its solar panel products. R refers to the 'former' and 'latter' products mentioned in Q. P adds information about improvements in Tesla's panels.

parts.label: P
parts.text: The team of researchers in Nottingham refined the equation using new data and assumptions.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: They found that there are likely between four and 211 civilizations capable of communicating with others, with 36 the most likely number.

parts.label: R
parts.text: Our current technology makes it nearly impossible to detect or communicate with possible alien life.

parts.label: S
parts.text: Finding these civilizations is another issue entirely — scientists said they would be thousands of light years away.

items.explanation: P introduces the research. Q presents the findings. S discusses the challenge of locating these civilizations. R concludes by explaining why current technology makes communication difficult.

parts.label: P
parts.text: Considering the large volume of Bangladeshi migrants in the Middle East, secondary economic impacts through depressed demand and falling oil prices will also likely add strain to the flow of remittances.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: But the COVID-19 pandemic is having an acute effect on Bangladeshi migrants abroad, who are largely concentrated in countries with strict lockdown measures.

parts.label: R
parts.text: International remittances normally represent around 7% of Bangladesh's GDP.

parts.label: S
parts.text: The economic importance of the more than 10 million migrants from Bangladesh who sent close to $18 billion in 2019 cannot be overstated.

items.explanation: S introduces the significance of migrant workers. R supports this with remittance statistics. Q introduces the impact of COVID-19. P elaborates on the economic consequences.

parts.label: P
parts.text: Studies on small cats remain limited with carnivore research in India being skewed towards large cats.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: Small cats are more specialized than their larger cousins in terms of resource selection.

parts.label: R
parts.text: We estimated the abundance of two widespread small cats, the jungle cat and the rusty-spotted cat, and investigated their habitat associations based on camera trap captures from a central Indian tiger reserve.

parts.label: S
parts.text: Studies on small cat population and habitat preference are critical to evaluate their status to ensure better management and conservation.

items.explanation: P introduces the research gap. Q highlights a characteristic of small cats. S explains why studying them is important. R concludes with the specific study undertaken.

rc.title: Reading Comprehension
rc.directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. Choose the most appropriate option.
rc.passage: No showpiece event of a sport has lived up to its billing quite like the FIFA World Cup. The 2026 edition, which kicks off on Thursday, offers proof. With 48 teams and 104 matches, it is the biggest ever. With roughly one in four FIFA member nations qualifying, and six of the seven continents represented, it is the most inclusive yet. From Oceania to North America, it wraps the whole universe. It is also the first time that three countries will be hosting the quadrennial extravaganza — the United States, Canada and Mexico. Top players in Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Neymar have touched down, and so have coaches such as Carlo Ancelotti and Thomas Tuchel. While Messi will aim for a repeat of Argentina’s trophy-winning exploits from 2022, Ronaldo will gun for Portugal’s first. Neymar, yet to win the coveted Cup, has a very heavy cross to bear, for he comes from the land of Pele and five-time champion Brazil. Kylian Mbappe’s France, titlist in 2018 and runner-up in 2022, remains strong. Spain, with the irresistible teenager Lamine Yamal in its ranks, is a favourite, and so are Germany and England to a lesser degree. But four-time winner Italy is absent, for a scarcely believable third straight occasion.

questions.question: Q1. According to the passage, what makes the FIFA World Cup 2026 the most inclusive edition till date?
options: It is being hosted by three countries
It has 48 teams, with nearly one-fourth FIFA nations qualifying and six continents represented
It includes legendary players and coaches
It features the highest number of matches in World Cup history
questions.answer: It has 48 teams, with nearly one-fourth FIFA nations qualifying and six continents represented
questions.explanation: The passage specifically states that the 2026 World Cup is the most inclusive because roughly one in four FIFA member nations qualify and six of the seven continents are represented.

questions.question: Q2. Which of the following statements is TRUE according to the passage?
options: Italy has qualified for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
Portugal has previously won the FIFA World Cup.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico.
Neymar has already won a FIFA World Cup with Brazil.
questions.answer: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico.
questions.explanation: The passage clearly mentions that for the first time three countries — the United States, Canada and Mexico — will jointly host the tournament.

questions.question: Q3. The phrase 'a very heavy cross to bear' as used in the passage most nearly means:
questions.explanation: The phrase is used to indicate the pressure on Neymar to win the World Cup for Brazil, a nation with a rich footballing legacy.

questions.question: Q4. Why does the author mention Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Neymar in the passage?
options: To highlight the star power and global appeal of the tournament
To explain the qualification process for the World Cup
questions.answer: To highlight the star power and global appeal of the tournament
questions.explanation: The mention of these world-famous players emphasizes the prestige, popularity and attraction of the FIFA World Cup.

questions.question: Q5. Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: Italy has failed to qualify for the FIFA World Cup for the third consecutive time.
France is no longer considered a strong team.
Spain has never won the FIFA World Cup.
All seven continents are represented in the 2026 World Cup.
questions.answer: Italy has failed to qualify for the FIFA World Cup for the third consecutive time.
questions.explanation: The passage states that four-time winner Italy is absent for a 'third straight occasion', implying three consecutive failures to qualify.

cloze.title: Cloze Test
cloze.directions: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Choose the correct answer for each question.
cloze.passage: Twenty three Opposition parties aligned under the banner of the INDIA bloc met in the national capital against the backdrop of economic distress, inflation and chaos in the educational sector. The bloc resolved to write to the Chief Justice of India over concerns of electoral fraud and vote (1)______. It also demanded the immediate resignation of the Union Education Minister and called upon the government to convene an all-party meeting to address the deepening economic crisis, farm distress and price (2)______. The parties agreed to hold coordination meetings every two months and committed to daily parliamentary coordination during sessions. These decisions signal a collective (3)______ to press the ruling party on governance failures and maintain Opposition unity. However, the meeting followed evident (4)______ within the alliance that surfaced during recent Assembly elections. The absence of the DMK further highlighted internal tensions after a bitter political (5)______ in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Blank (1):
questions.explanation: The phrase 'electoral fraud and vote manipulation' is contextually correct. The other options do not fit the idea of electoral malpractice.

questions.question: Blank (2):
questions.explanation: 'Price rise' is a standard expression referring to inflation. The other options contradict the context.

questions.question: Blank (3):
questions.explanation: 'Collective resolve' means a firm determination, which fits the context of coordinated political action.

questions.question: Blank (4):
questions.explanation: 'Fissures' means divisions or cracks within a group, matching the context of internal disagreements.

questions.question: Blank (5):
questions.explanation: 'Political fallout' refers to negative consequences or conflict arising from political events, which best fits the passage.

parajumble.title: Para Jumbles
parajumble.directions: Each sentence has been split into four parts (P, Q, R, S) given in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges them into a meaningful sentence.

parts.label: P

parts.label: Q

parts.label: R

parts.label: S

items.explanation: R introduces Oliver's feeling after recovery. S explains the reason as the crisis is over. P follows naturally because he feels connected to life again. Q concludes with his gradual physical recovery.

parts.label: S
parts.text: So one day he invited the crane for dinner and served the dishes on a plate.

items.explanation: R introduces the fox's intention. S shows his action. Q explains why the crane could not eat and introduces the crane's turn. P concludes with the crane's revenge and the fox's inability to eat.

parts.label: P
parts.text: But for spiritual knowledge mere memory of holy texts will be of no use in passing the tests.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: One can score in them by the power of memory.

parts.label: R
parts.text: A competent guru alone can provide the necessary guidance to an earnest disciple.

parts.label: S

items.explanation: Q refers to school examinations mentioned in the opening sentence. P contrasts spiritual knowledge with ordinary exams. S explains what is actually required. R adds the role of a competent guru.

parts.label: P

parts.label: Q

parts.label: S

items.explanation: R explains why the peasant is important. P logically concludes that he is useful to society. Q contrasts this by highlighting his exploitation. S follows as the moral conclusion.

parts.label: P
parts.text: She was shown the corner where the gum bottle was kept.

parts.label: Q

parts.label: R

parts.label: S
parts.text: She thanked the lady and came to the counter on the left extreme and got the stamps.

items.explanation: Q follows the opening sentence as Priya is redirected. S shows that she gets the stamps. R introduces her next need for gum. P explains where she finds it before posting the letter.

rc.title: Reading Comprehension
rc.directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. Choose the most appropriate option.
rc.passage: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies of the 21st century. It enables machines to perform tasks that traditionally required human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, problem-solving and decision-making. AI is now widely used in healthcare, education, transportation, banking and entertainment. In healthcare, AI-powered systems assist doctors in diagnosing diseases more accurately and quickly. In education, personalized learning platforms help students learn at their own pace. Businesses use AI to analyze large volumes of data and improve efficiency. However, the rapid growth of AI has also raised concerns regarding job displacement, privacy and ethical decision-making. Experts believe that while AI may replace certain routine tasks, it will also create new opportunities and industries. Therefore, the challenge lies in using AI responsibly so that its benefits can be enjoyed by society while minimizing potential risks.

questions.question: Q1. According to the passage, what is one of the main reasons AI is considered transformative?
options: It can completely replace human beings.
It enables machines to perform tasks requiring human intelligence.
It is only useful in the healthcare sector.
It eliminates the need for education.
questions.answer: It enables machines to perform tasks requiring human intelligence.
questions.explanation: The passage states that AI allows machines to perform tasks such as learning, reasoning, problem-solving and decision-making, which traditionally required human intelligence.

questions.question: Q2. Which of the following fields is NOT mentioned in the passage as using AI?
questions.explanation: The passage mentions healthcare, education, transportation, banking and entertainment, but does not mention agriculture.

questions.question: Q3. What concern related to AI is highlighted in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage specifically mentions concerns regarding job displacement, privacy and ethical decision-making.

questions.question: Q4. What do experts believe about the future impact of AI on employment?
options: AI will only create jobs and never replace any.
AI may replace some routine tasks but will also create new opportunities.
AI will have no effect on employment.
questions.answer: AI may replace some routine tasks but will also create new opportunities.
questions.explanation: The passage states that experts believe AI will replace certain routine tasks while also creating new opportunities and industries.

questions.question: Q5. Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: AI should be banned because it is dangerous.
The benefits of AI can be maximized through responsible use.
AI is only beneficial for large businesses.
Privacy concerns related to AI have already been solved.
questions.answer: The benefits of AI can be maximized through responsible use.
questions.explanation: The passage concludes that AI should be used responsibly so that society can enjoy its benefits while minimizing risks.

rc.title: Reading Comprehension
rc.directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. Choose the most appropriate option.
rc.passage: India is located between two major drug-producing regions: Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Iran to the west and Myanmar, Thailand, and Laos to the east. While the West has historically dominated heroin production, the International Narcotics Control Board has said Myanmar has become the world’s leading source of illicit opium while East and Southeast Asia remain major sources of methamphetamine. Officials have said drugs are being received at Gujarat, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu via maritime routes. Similarly, some drugs are produced domestically using illegally diverted pharmaceutical ingredients, aided by the fact that individuals possessing small quantities of heroin can attract up to six months’ imprisonment, whereas drugmakers that cannot account for lakhs of doses often face only slaps on the wrist. The rise of Myanmar, where the territory under ethnic armed organisations is expanding, as a key source is also troubling since it shares a border with India. The Narcotics Control Bureau has noted a dramatic surge in the use of drones to smuggle drugs across borders, especially over Punjab. Traffickers are organising over the darknet and using cryptocurrencies. The pillars of India’s response thus aim to keep the enforcement regime from being out-innovated and improve regulatory certainty.

questions.question: Q1. According to the passage, why is India particularly vulnerable to drug trafficking?
options: It is located between two major drug-producing regions.
It has the world's largest pharmaceutical industry.
It shares borders only with Myanmar.
questions.answer: It is located between two major drug-producing regions.
questions.explanation: The passage states that India lies between major drug-producing regions to its west and east, making it particularly vulnerable to drug trafficking.

questions.question: Q2. According to the International Narcotics Control Board, which country has become the world's leading source of illicit opium?
questions.explanation: The passage mentions that Myanmar has become the world's leading source of illicit opium.

questions.question: Q3. Which method of drug smuggling has witnessed a dramatic increase according to the Narcotics Control Bureau?
questions.explanation: The passage highlights a dramatic surge in the use of drones to smuggle drugs across borders, especially over Punjab.

questions.question: Q4. Which of the following technologies are traffickers using to organize and facilitate drug trafficking?
questions.explanation: The passage states that traffickers are organising over the darknet and using cryptocurrencies.

questions.question: Q5. What is the primary objective of India's response to the growing drug menace, according to the passage?
options: To increase imprisonment for all drug users
To ensure enforcement keeps pace with evolving trafficking methods and improve regulatory certainty
To ban the use of drones across the country
questions.answer: To ensure enforcement keeps pace with evolving trafficking methods and improve regulatory certainty
questions.explanation: The passage concludes that India's response focuses on preventing the enforcement regime from being out-innovated while improving regulatory certainty.

cloze.title: Cloze Test
cloze.directions: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Choose the correct answer for each question.
cloze.passage: India is located between two major drug-producing regions: Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Iran to the west and Myanmar, Thailand, and Laos to the east. While the West has historically dominated heroin production, Myanmar has become the world's leading source of illicit (1)______. Officials have stated that drugs are being received through maritime routes at Gujarat, Kerala, and (2)______. The Narcotics Control Bureau has also noted a dramatic surge in the use of (3)______ to smuggle drugs across borders, especially over Punjab. Traffickers are increasingly organising over the (4)______ and using cryptocurrencies. India's response aims to ensure that its enforcement regime is not out-innovated while improving regulatory (5)______.

questions.question: Blank (1):
questions.explanation: Myanmar has become the world's leading source of illicit opium, making 'opium' the correct answer.

questions.question: Blank (2):
questions.explanation: The passage mentions Gujarat, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu as key maritime entry points for drugs.

questions.question: Blank (3):
questions.explanation: The Narcotics Control Bureau has reported a sharp increase in the use of drones for cross-border drug smuggling.

questions.question: Blank (4):
questions.explanation: Drug traffickers increasingly organise over the darknet and use cryptocurrencies for illicit activities.

questions.question: Blank (5):
questions.explanation: India's response seeks to improve regulatory certainty while strengthening enforcement against evolving drug trafficking methods.

parajumble.title: Para Jumbles
parajumble.directions: Each sentence has been split into four parts (P, Q, R, S) given in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges them into a meaningful sentence.

parts.label: P
parts.text: However, alongside the celebrations, public debates have also emerged regarding donations, land transactions and fund management.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: The Ram Mandir in Ayodhya is one of the most significant religious and cultural developments in modern India.

parts.label: R
parts.text: These discussions have led some critics to use the phrase 'Ram Mandir loot'.

parts.label: S
parts.text: For millions of devotees, it represents the fulfillment of a centuries-old aspiration.

items.explanation: Q introduces the topic. S explains its significance. P introduces the contrasting debates. R concludes with the result of those debates.

parts.label: P
parts.text: Large religious projects involving substantial public donations naturally attract scrutiny.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: It is important to distinguish between verified facts and unproven allegations.

parts.label: R
parts.text: Some groups have demanded greater transparency in financial records and procurement.

parts.label: S
parts.text: The temple trust has rejected allegations of wrongdoing and stated that procedures were properly followed.

items.explanation: Q establishes the principle of separating facts from allegations. P explains why scrutiny exists. R mentions demands for transparency. S presents the response of the temple trust.

parts.label: P
parts.text: Property prices increased, tourism expanded and new businesses emerged.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: The rapid development of Ayodhya has transformed the city's economy.

parts.label: R
parts.text: However, some residents have expressed concerns about rising costs and displacement.

parts.label: S
parts.text: These concerns highlight the challenges associated with large development projects.

items.explanation: Q introduces the economic transformation. P provides examples of development. R presents the contrasting concerns. S concludes with the broader implication.

parts.label: P
parts.text: Unfortunately, some criminals exploit religious sentiments through fake donation drives.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: The phrase 'Ram Mandir loot' is also used in another context.

parts.label: R
parts.text: They may impersonate temple representatives or create fraudulent online campaigns.

parts.label: S
parts.text: Therefore, devotees should contribute only through officially recognized channels.

items.explanation: Q introduces the alternate meaning of the phrase. P explains the fraud. R describes the methods used by fraudsters. S ends with the precautionary advice.

parts.label: P
parts.text: Independent audits and clear financial disclosures can strengthen public confidence.

parts.label: Q
parts.text: Transparency is essential for maintaining public trust in institutions managing donated funds.

parts.label: R
parts.text: At the same time, criticism should be based on credible evidence rather than rumours.

parts.label: S
parts.text: Such a balanced approach respects both public accountability and religious faith.

items.explanation: Q introduces the importance of transparency. P explains how transparency can be achieved. R stresses responsible criticism. S concludes with the balanced outcome.
